date_windows.applies_to: population reference date; publication/retrieval dates are provenance, not observations

frozen_payload.notes: Selected first because the public source is complete for the bounded question, table and codelist semantics are auditable, the main alternative explanations have observable negative controls, data cost is zero, and the claim ceiling is independent of any preferred causal model. 'Impact on consciousness' is not an outcome. This specification authorises no new human-participant research.
frozen_payload.objective: Estimate how sensitive the England and Wales Census 2021 gender-identity response statistics and selected subgroup contrasts are to response-category construction, nonresponse, proxy response, language-comprehension indicators and denominator choice, without estimating latent true prevalence or any individual causal effect.
frozen_payload.planned_analysis: 1. Re-retrieve the frozen table set after the committed freeze and record canonical URL, query, retrieval time, source version and SHA-256 for every response. 2. Build and publish the codelist/denominator crosswalk before computing estimates. 3. Estimate the prespecified category-definition ratio and absolute difference, denominator sensitivities, nonresponse contrasts and observable language/comprehension-related contrasts with perturbation limits stated. 4. Run the same-form sexual-orientation negative control where definitionally valid. 5. Apply the frozen materiality rule: a relative difference of at least 20% or an absolute difference of at least 0.10 percentage points in a headline response proportion is material; report estimates and uncertainty rather than dichotomising when perturbation prevents a decision. 6. Run denominator, category-recode and table-perturbation sensitivity analyses. 7. Publish regardless of direction. No model converts these aggregate response statistics into individual exposure, identity-origin, psychological or consciousness claims.
frozen_payload.primary_outcome: Published proportion responding that gender identity differs from sex registered at birth, under each frozen denominator/category definition; this is a response statistic, not latent true prevalence.

scope.construct: sensitivity of published gender-identity response statistics to observable instrument and response-process features
scope.estimand: (1) prespecified prevalence ratios and risk differences for a published 'gender identity different from sex registered at birth' response across observable comprehension/nonresponse strata; (2) the ratio and absolute difference produced by the two published codelists that attach 'all other gender identities' to different category contents; and (3) a sensitivity interval for the published national response proportion under frozen denominator and suspect-response recodes
scope.jurisdiction: England and Wales, with Scotland used only in a separately harmonised sensitivity analysis
scope.period: 2021-03-21 Census reference date; confirmatory retrieval after specification freeze
scope.population: usual residents aged 16 and over in England and Wales on the Census 2021 reference date

search_concepts.concept: Census 2021 gender-identity response tables and prespecified cross-tabs
question wording, response process, uncertainty and regulatory status
query_terms: quality of Census 2021 gender identity data

selection_rules.description: Use only official published cells whose geography, age eligibility, gender-identity codelist, denominator role and observation status are explicitly resolved.
Use the published total cell for a denominator or margin; never derive it by summing a codelist that contains its own totals or nested aggregates.
Treat sexual-orientation response behaviour on the same form as a negative-control instrument, not as an exposure or causal covariate.
Exclude structural zeros, suppressed/non-normal cells and any cell whose codelist or denominator cannot be resolved before analysis.
The 2026-08-16 harvest is excluded from confirmatory status because it predates this freeze; it may inform source semantics and test fixtures only.
Do not interpret cross-sectional age gradients as trends or census sex response as a verified measure of sex registered at birth.
